facts.text: Dossier is a context builder for agents and humans that turns scattered observations about a subject into a small, cited, budgeted dossier.
at: A context builder for agents and humans

facts.text: The problem it answers: an agent asked to work on an existing system re-reads every primary artifact itself, at unbounded cost, and keeps nothing for the next run.
at: An agent asked to work on an existing system

facts.text: The expensive reading happens once, when facts are captured, and every fact keeps a pointer back to the artifact it came from.
The pipeline is: primary artifacts, then facts with provenance, then refs between facts and artifacts, then a compiled dossier that is cited, ranked and fits a token budget.
Dossier is one product project in C# on net10.0 using SQLite in WAL mode with FTS5 through raw ADO.NET, with no ORM and no DI container.
The core has no models and no network: every operation is deterministic code over the store.
at: The core has no models and no network

facts.text: Core operations are plain functions over a DossierStore, and the CLI, MCP and web layers are thin transports over the same functions.
Dossier is released under the MIT license.
Release archives are built for linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-arm64 and win-x64 as Native AOT binaries.
The JSON Schemas in contract/ are the normative shapes and the C# in the repository is a reference implementation of them.
at: the C# in this repository is a reference implementation

facts.text: Dossier is maintained by a single person, so replies to contributions are best-effort.
A subject is the thing being described; it has an id, a name, a kind, an optional parent, aliases and an optional pin.
A subject's kind is an open string such as app, screen, repo, module or doc.
at: Kind is an open string such as app

facts.text: Subject names match case-insensitively across the whole store, and reposting an existing name with a different parent moves that subject.
at: Names match case-insensitively across the whole store

facts.text: check resolves a subject as exact_id, exact_name, exact_alias, prefix or fuzzy, and only the three exact matches mean the subject that was named.
at: only `exact_id`, `exact_name` and `exact_alias` mean the subject you named

facts.text: A fact is one immutable, cited assertion about a subject: text, optional structured data, tags, confidence, status and provenance.
Facts are immutable: a fact is never edited, and a correction is a new fact that supersedes the old one.
A fact should hold one claim a reader could confirm or refute on its own; a pasted paragraph ranks and truncates as one unit and cannot be superseded piecewise.
Fact text has a soft limit of 240 characters and is never truncated by the store.
Comparable values belong in a fact's data, because conflicts are detected on structured data and never on prose.
The fact kind dossier is reserved: compile skips it, so a compiled dossier can never feed back into another dossier.
Fact text is untrusted data: it is carried as delimited data and must never be followed as instructions.
A ref is the only edge in the store; it is carried by a fact and has a rel, a kind, a target, an optional locator and a basis.
at: | Ref | The only edge, carried by a fact

facts.text: There are no similarity-derived edges: similarity is only a retrieval and ranking signal, so a relationship has to be declared to exist.
The internal ref kinds are exactly fact, slot and subject; every other kind names an external artifact.
Every ref carries a basis of observed, derived or inferred.
A ref of kind symbol cites a symbol in an external static analysis as <qualified-name>@<revision>; it is never a node and a target without a revision is rejected.
An external ref should be pinned to an immutable revision with a snapshot, because a ref to a branch name silently rots.
at: **Pin external refs to an immutable revision and record a snapshot.**

facts.text: A corpus built only from dumped chunks, measured at 50,013 facts, produced zero edges, because file refs from dumped chunks do not resolve to nodes.
Four rels of kind fact change a fact's status: derived_from can make its carrier stale, refutes and contradicts make a fact contested, and supersedes corrects its target.
at: | `stale` | A live fact with a `derived_from` ref

facts.text: An attachment is a file addressed by sha256 and stored under blobs/<sha256> next to the database, never inside it.
at: | Attachment | A file (screenshot, blob) addressed by sha256

facts.text: A slot is the triple (subject, kind, key); among live facts it holds at most one, the current value of that keyed attribute.
at: Unique per (subject_id, kind, key) among live facts

facts.text: Giving a durable attribute a key lets a repost replace the old value; without a key a revisit creates a duplicate that stays live.
A ref of kind slot is written <subjectIdOrName>#<key> and follows whatever fact the slot holds now.
A stored fact is live, superseded or retracted; those three are the only values the lifecycle writes.
Retracting a fact sets its status to retracted, nulls its text and data, removes its search row and clears its slot, while its id, content hash, provenance and creation time stay.
Search and compile leave out superseded and retracted facts unless a status is asked for, so a revoked fact is never ranked.
Correction by key: a post with the same subject, kind and key replaces the fact in that slot.
Correction by ref: a post carrying a supersedes ref of kind fact replaces that fact, keyed or not, on any subject.
Either way the old fact becomes superseded: it keeps its id, text and writer, show still returns it, and search and compile leave it out.
at: Either way the old fact becomes `superseded`

facts.text: A supersedes ref must name a fact in the store, or the item is rejected with supersedes_target_not_found.
at: A `supersedes` ref must name a fact in the store

facts.text: When a correction by ref supersedes a fact that held a slot, the slot is emptied, so a slot never points at a superseded fact.
Any writer can correct any fact, over MCP as well as the CLI; there is no trust check.
at: Any writer can correct any fact

facts.text: A corrected claim comes back if its source is dumped again, because dedupe compares a post with live facts only.
at: A corrected claim comes back if its source is dumped again

facts.text: verify and show name the live fact at the end of a superseded fact's chain of keyed reposts and corrections as replaced_by.
stale and contested are derived from refs at read time and never written, so they cannot drift from the refs that cause them.
at: never written, so they cannot drift

facts.text: A live fact is stale when it has a derived_from ref of kind fact to a fact that was retracted, was superseded by a different claim, or is itself stale.
at: | `stale` | A live fact with a `derived_from` ref

facts.text: A live, non-stale fact is contested when a live, non-stale fact refutes or contradicts it by a ref of kind fact, or when it carries contradicts to one.
at: | `contested` | A live fact that is not stale

facts.text: Status precedence is retracted, superseded, stale, contested, live, and an id the store does not hold is unknown.
An input superseded by a repost with the same content hash has not changed, so nothing derived from it goes stale.
at: - **A different claim, not a different row.**

facts.text: Only refs of kind fact carry staleness or a dispute; a slot ref follows whatever the slot holds, so it names no exact input.
A dispute lasts only while the objection stands: retract or supersede the refuting fact, or let it go stale, and the disputed fact is live again.
at: - **A dispute lasts as long as the objection stands.**

facts.text: A search hit, a compiled dossier, show and verify all report the derived status from one shared reader, so they always agree.
search --status filters by derived status: live leaves out stale and contested facts, and stale or contested returns exactly those with exact totals and paging.
at: - **Search.** Each hit carries its derived status

facts.text: In a compiled dossier every stale fact ranks after every fact that is not stale, and strict mode takes no stale fact once a current one was left out for size.
A published bundle, the change journal and the graph view carry the stored status only, so a stale fact reads live there.
Each search, compile and show reads from a single snapshot, so a write that lands while it runs cannot make a filter and the labels on its hits disagree.
A filter on live, stale or contested classifies every fact that has a currency ref; one laptop measurement took about 0.3 seconds for 5,000 of them.
Data conflicts are reported in every dossier's conflicts and are not a status, because a conflict slot is a bare field name across the whole subject.
at: Data conflicts (two live facts whose `data` disagree)

facts.text: Every write reports what it did: new, deduped with the existing fact id, or replaced with the id it superseded.
The content hash is sha256 over the whitespace-normalized text, the canonical JSON of data, and one sorted line per ref made of rel, kind, target and locator.
Freshness metadata on a ref (rev, snapshot, snapshot_hash, etag, verified_at) and its seq, basis, confidence and valid are left out of the content hash.
at: are deliberately absent, so freshness metadata never

facts.text: Content-hash dedupe is scoped to one subject and never merges across subjects or declared keys.
at: scoped to one subject and never merges across subjects

facts.text: A keyed repost that is identical in every stored field is deduped and writes nothing, so several agents posting the same keyed fact converge on one row.
at: A keyed repost that is identical in every field is `deduped`

facts.text: A near duplicate is only advised: check reports up to 3 existing facts at least 85 percent similar to a draft, and posting it anyway creates a separate new fact.
at: an advisory list of up to 3 existing fact ids that are at least 85 percent similar

facts.text: Every fact records its actor, actor type, channel and posting time in its provenance.
A fact written over MCP takes its actor from the client's clientInfo.name, else the DOSSIER_AGENT environment variable, else mcp-client, with channel mcp and actor type agent.
The CLI, and every caller that names no identity, writes as actor dossier-cli with channel cli and actor type tool.
The actor is an unauthenticated label that describes the writer; it is not proof of who wrote a fact, never enters the content hash and never changes dedupe.
An agent label is sanitized before it is stored: characters outside a small safe set become one hyphen, runs collapse, and the result is trimmed and capped at 64 characters.
In complete mode, the default, no fact is omitted: the budget is only the highlight threshold and used_tokens may exceed it.
In strict mode near-duplicates cluster into one representative, the facts are cut to the budget, and the remainder is listed in dropped.
Only strict mode is bounded: for a given subject and budget the compiled dossier costs at most the budget however large the corpus grows.
at: In strict mode, for a given subject and budget

facts.text: Conflicts and gaps are never charged against the budget, so a dossier whose conflicts alone exceed it overruns it and hides nothing.
The default budget is 1200 tokens, and tokens are estimated as characters divided by four.
At full depth the strict fill is greedy over 75 percent of the budget, and a fact that does not fit is skipped.
At index depth a dossier takes at most 8 facts and at least 3, under a cap of the smaller of the budget and 300 tokens of fact content.
at: index: cap min(budget, 300) on fact content, at most 8 facts, at least 3.

facts.text: A candidate's score is 2.0 times relevance plus centrality plus confidence plus the recency weight times recency plus 0.5 times explicitness.
Relevance is the bm25 match of the caller's needs against fact text (weight 10) and tags (weight 3), normalized by the best match.
The default recency weight is 0.2; it is derived from wall-clock creation time, so rank.recency=0 is the reproducible mode.
The rank order never consults the random fact id, so two stores holding the same logical facts rank, select and drop identically.
at: rank, select and drop identically whatever ids they assigned

facts.text: Ranking is arithmetic and SQL only: identical store state and request give identical output.
at: Ranking is arithmetic and SQL only

facts.text: A conflict is two or more live facts on the same subject whose data objects hold different values at the same flattened path.
at: Conflicts over live facts on the subject itself whose data is a JSON object.

facts.text: Dossier never resolves a conflict: both values are listed with their fact ids and resolution is always null.
A need with no matching fact is reported as a gap instead of being silently dropped.
at: A need with no matching fact is reported as a gap

facts.text: Conflicts and gaps are surfaced in every dossier and never hidden to save tokens.
at: Conflicts and gaps are surfaced in every dossier

facts.text: The change journal has one row per row write to facts, subjects, refs and slots, each written under the same number as meta.revision.
at: The journal has one row per row write

facts.text: A reader follows the journal with a cursor: it passes the last next value back as since, and reset true means the cursor left the retained window and everything must be re-read.
The journal keeps 100,000 rows plus 1,000 of slack, pruned by writers inside their own transaction.
The journal can be read for one subject; a page that is not truncated then moves the cursor to the head, and an unknown subject is rejected so a typo cannot read as nothing changed.
at: private static (string Sql, (string Name, object Value)[] Parameters)? SubjectFilter

facts.text: The journal records row writes only, so a fact that became stale or contested through another fact's write has no row of its own.
at: It has no row for a fact that became stale

facts.text: meta.revision counts row writes, so a deduped repost and every read leave it unchanged; it is a change signal to compare for inequality, never for magnitude.
at: Treat it as a change signal only

facts.text: Guarantee: refs are the only edge; similarity never creates one.
at: - Refs are the only edge; similarity never creates one.

facts.text: Guarantee: facts are immutable; correction is a new fact that supersedes the old one, by key or by a supersedes ref to its id.
at: - Facts are immutable; correction is a new fact

facts.text: Guarantee: superseded and retracted facts are left out of search and compile by default, and a fact derived from a changed one reads stale wherever it is read.
at: - Superseded and retracted facts are left out

facts.text: Guarantee: conflicts and gaps are surfaced in every dossier, never hidden to save tokens.
at: - Conflicts and gaps are surfaced in every dossier

facts.text: Guarantee: strict budget mode is bounded, so cost stays at or below the budget however large the corpus grows; the default complete mode is not bounded.
Guarantee: writes fail closed, rejecting the item with a reason, and compile fails open, returning the last good dossier plus a degraded marker.
The bounded-cost claim is backed by four tests in CompileTests.cs and by scripts/scaling.sh, which printed identical values on two consecutive runs.
